projectRefs: The moons silent witness   When humans first arrived here, the whole world was so excited. Millions of people had gathered in front of their televisions. I will never forget those hopeful looks of the humans... They were watching me with excitement, holding their breath in silence, as if even the tiniest sound would break all the magic.   I safely carried all the astronauts through that unknown, pitch-black space. For a few hours, I became a home to each of them. And I watched with great excitement as they took their first steps. Everything was going so well until my mission was over.   I didn't know yet that the footprints they left behind, the American flag that couldn't wave because there is no wind, and the batteries they left would remain my only friends. As they returned to my bright blue and lush green home, I had to watch them with a deep sense of heartbreak and sadness.   After they left, everything started to feel so empty. Whenever I looked at that azure planet, my heart ached. Because there is no wind, time felt like it stopped moving.   For more than fifty years, there has been no sound of laughter here, no human voice on a radio, and no roar of an engine.   This place is actually like a quiet, open-air history museum. Just a few steps away from me, the American flag still stands in all its glory; it hasn't felt the touch of wind for a long, long time. A little further out, you can see the deep bootprints, looking just as fresh and solid as they did on day one.   Nowadays, scientists call us "space junk." How quickly they forgot that we are the proof of humanity's greatest achievements! Yet, on day one, our value was priceless.   I believe we are definitely not worthless enough to be called mere "trash"! How can we be compared to the dirt down on Earth? We are the greatest proof of human courage. We are the ones who allowed humans to see the places they once looked up at in the night sky with wonder and curiosity. How could they have ever reached these places without us?   The fact that they invented us doesn't give them the right to forget us by simply calling us trash. How quickly they forgot how hard they struggled and how much effort they put into overcoming every challenge while inventing us.   Here we are, standing tall just like on day one alongside my silent friends across the Moon. We are looking back at our home—that home with its azure rivers, lonely deserts, oceans that shelter all water life, lush plains, and bountiful forests. We are safely keeping their memories alive.   Who knows? Maybe one day people will come back to visit us, remember our true value, and build a museum for us. And make us eternal.
